newsitem.title: USA: Albany Cty, NY official rejects $110 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Albany Cty, NY official rejects $110 mln bond sale.

text.p: The Albany County Comptroller on Thursday rejected a $110 million airport bond offering due to concerns about the negotiated aspect of the sale, as well as the issues' 30-year maturity, local airport officials said.

"The Albany County Comptroller today declined to approve the Authority's financing package. He objects, I understand to the negotiated sale aspect and the 30-year term," said Harry Robinson, chairman of the Albany County Airport Authority, in prepared remarks.
The authority had planned to sell the bonds next week to finance a $158 million expansion that had been unanimously approved by the Albany County Airport Authority.
Robinson said that the Authority was exploring its financing options in the wake of the decision by the comptroller, Michael Conners.

A spokesman, Peter Cutler, for the Authority said these options include a sale of 90-day bond anticipation notes, which then might be followed by a negotiated sale, but he noted that some financial advisors have said this course is not feasible. No timeframe for when the Authority would make its decision was disclosed. "Frankly, I don't know, it's really throwing a monkey wrench in there."

The county comptroller, in a letter to the Authority, told it that a competitive bond sale would not require his approval, but the airport wants to sell the bonds on a negotiated basis because this would be its first issue, the airport official said. He added the 30-year term was chosen because it matches the life of the capital improvements, and would result in lower borrowing costs.
